title: On-screen display overlay for current zoom state
description:
Custom OSD (on-screen display) overlay that shows the current zoom preset as a gauge when rotating between presets.

Visual feedback for zoom rotation — a transient overlay that appears briefly showing where you are in the zoom spectrum. Like a volume OSD but for window height emphasis.

## Design

- Gauge/bar showing the active flex_grow position on the spectrum
- Preset name label
- Transient: appears on rotation, fades after a short timeout
- Lightweight: no heavy toolkit dependency, likely a simple wlr-layer-surface or similar

## Acceptance Criteria

- OSD overlay appears on zoom rotation events
- Shows current preset name and position on the zoom spectrum as a gauge
- Transient display with fade timeout
- Minimal dependencies

title: Niri keybindings for vicinae extension actions
description:
Niri keybindings that invoke vicinae extension actions — the launcher UI for zoom preset selection and other zk operations.

Rather than binding keys directly to zk CLI commands (zk-niri-keybindings), these bindings open the vicinae launcher filtered to zk commands, giving a visual selection interface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Niri keybindings that open vicinae with zk extension commands
- Keybinding to open vicinae filtered to zoom presets
- Documented config snippets

title: Vicinae extension for zk zoom management
description:
Build a vicinae (linux raycast launcher, TypeScript) extension providing commands for browsing and activating zoom presets, inspecting current state, etc.

## Commands

- List zoom presets with current state highlighted
- Activate a zoom preset by name
- Show current zoom state and where it sits in the rotation order
- Rotate next/prev through presets

Vicinae is a linux port of raycast, programmed in TypeScript. The extension would communicate with zk via its CLI interface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Vicinae extension package structure
- Commands for listing, selecting, and rotating zoom presets
- Integration with zk CLI for state queries

title: Expose zk operations as niri keybindable commands
description:
Create niri keybinding integration for zk operations. Niri keybindings call zk CLI commands directly.

## Keybindings

- `zk zoom rotate --next` / `--prev` bound to key combos for cycling zoom presets
- `zk zoom set <name>` for direct preset activation
- Other zk subcommands as appropriate

This requires zk CLI commands to be fast and self-contained (niri keybindings spawn processes, not long-running daemons).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documented niri keybinding config snippets
- zk CLI responds quickly enough for interactive keybinding use
- Keybindings for zoom rotation (next/prev)
- Keybindings for common zoom presets

title: Dbus notification layer for zk actions
description:
Add a dbus notification system that reports on actions done by the zk toolsuite.

## v1: Notifications

Emit dbus notifications on zk actions:
- Zoom preset changed (which preset, previous state)
- Focus events
- Window layout changes
- Any zk CLI action

## v2: MCP-like Resource URIs

Ship MCP-style resource URIs that reference events and expose action potentials — callable operations on those resources. For example, a zoom-change notification could include a resource URI that other tools can resolve to inspect the event details and invoke actions (rotate back, set a different preset, etc.).

Action potentials are operations that can be run against the resource — the event becomes an object with affordances, not just a passive notification.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dbus notification emission on zk events
- Structured notification payload (event type, details, timestamp)
- v2: Resource URI scheme for events
- v2: Action potential definitions on event resources

title: CLI tool to rotate between zoom presets with previous-register
description:
Implement rotation between zoom presets with sorted ordering and previous-register behavior.

## Rotation Behavior

1. Zoom presets are sorted by `active` flex_grow ascending (e.g., `equal: 0.5` → `focused: 0.7` → `maximal: 0.9`)
2. `rotate --next` moves to the next higher active grow, `rotate --prev` to the next lower
3. Current state is located in the sorted order — if you're at `focused: 0.7`, `--next` goes to `maximal: 0.9`
4. If current state is ad-hoc (not a preset), it slots into the sorted order by its effective active ratio. If you're at `0.65` and rotate `--next`, you'd go to `focused: 0.7` (the next preset above). That ad-hoc `0.65` gets stashed as "previous" so `--prev` returns to it

The sort key is `active` flex_grow — the single axis of emphasis. Deterministic, no ambiguity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `zk zoom rotate --next` / `zk zoom rotate --prev` CLI subcommands
- Sorted rotation through presets
- Previous-register for ad-hoc states (rotate back to non-preset values)
- `zk zoom set <name>` to activate a named preset directly
- `zk zoom list` to show available presets with current indicated

title: Define zoom preset data model and config
description:
Define the "zoom" concept: a named preset of flex_grow active/other ratios that controls longcat height distribution.

A **zoom** is a named preset like `focused: { active: 0.7, other: 0.3 }`, `equal: { active: 0.5, other: 0.5 }`, `maximal: { active: 0.9, other: 0.1 }`. The existing zoomer adjusts font size; longcat zooms adjust height proportion. Each zoom preset is a pair of flex_grow values (active, other) that determine how column height is split between focused and unfocused windows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Zoom preset struct with name, active flex_grow, other flex_grow
- Config format for defining named presets (TOML)
- Default presets shipped (equal, focused, maximal)
- "Previous" register concept: when rotating away from an ad-hoc state (manual resize, non-preset values), that state is stashed for return
- Presets are sorted by active flex_grow for rotation ordering

title: Add optional process metadata enrichment for export records
description: Research and design optional process metadata enrichment for export records that have PIDs, especially window records. The initial goal is to expose useful process identity such as executable path/name, command line, and tmux-related context when the PID belongs to tmux.
design: This should be optional enrichment, not raw niri data. Decide where enriched data belongs: inline fields, an `enrichment`/`process` nested bag, or separate graph records. Prefer a nested bag initially to avoid confusing raw niri IPC fields with local OS-derived metadata. Investigate Linux /proc data availability for pid executable path, command line, process name, cwd, uid, parent pid, process group/session ids, start time, and whether the process is still alive. For tmux, research how to map a tmux client/server PID to session information. Possibilities include `tmux list-clients`, `tmux display-message`, socket paths, environment variables, or process tree inspection. Treat tmux metadata as volatile: it can change after export, and we should not imply it is stable unless refreshed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Research documents which process fields are useful and reliably available on Linux.
- Design specifies where enrichment is attached in export records.
- Design distinguishes raw niri fields from local enrichment.
- Tmux investigation identifies whether PID -> tmux session/client mapping is feasible and what command/API is needed.
- Notes cover stale data risks and permissions/failure cases.
- Follow-up implementation tasks are identified if enrichment is worth building.

title: Add graph and edge export mode
description: Explore and implement an export mode that represents niri state as a flat graph of typed node and edge records instead of only raw entity/event records. This should make relationships such as window -> workspace -> output and cast -> target explicit while preserving JSON/JSONL symmetry.
design:
Current export records are close to graph nodes already. A graph mode would add derived edge records such as workspace_on_output, window_on_workspace, window_in_column, workspace_active_window, layer_on_output, cast_targets_window, and cast_targets_output. Columns are derived nodes from `(workspace_id, column_idx)`, not raw niri entities, so graph mode must clearly mark derived records. Keep this separate from default raw export semantics unless the design proves the graph representation is a better default.

Also evaluate Open Canvas Interchange Format (OCIF) as a possible graph export target or parallel output mode. OCIF may be useful if we want niri state exports to be inspectable in canvas/graph tools rather than only line-oriented JSON consumers. Treat OCIF as an interoperability target to assess, not a default commitment.
acceptance_criteria:
- Define node and edge record shapes for JSON and JSONL.
- Document which records are raw niri entities and which are derived.
- Include edges for windows, workspaces, outputs, layers, and casts where data exists.
- Preserve stable record ordering where practical.
- Tests verify graph output for representative fixture data, including derived column edges.

title: Research facet-rs export serialization backend
description: Investigate whether facet-rs can be used as an export serialization backend alongside or instead of serde_json for niri export records, and whether it reduces adapter boilerplate or supports feature-gated serializer backends.
design: Research facet-rs capabilities with external types from niri_ipc, derived vs non-derived reflection, JSON output support, feature gating, and trait-based serializer abstraction. Compare against serde_json::Value, custom Serialize impls, and macro-generated adapters. Produce a recommendation before implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Research notes compare facet-rs with current serde implementation.
- Determine whether niri_ipc external types can be serialized without changing upstream.
- Identify required dependencies/features and binary impact concerns.
- Recommend whether to implement, defer, or reject facet backend.
- If recommended, outline the trait boundary for multiple export serializers.
notes:
2026-05-03 research result:
- Added optional dependencies `facet = 0.46` and `facet-json = 0.46` behind `export-facet`.
- Added `src/export/facet_json.rs` as the gated backend scaffold.
- `facet-json` requires values to implement `facet::Facet`.
- `niri_ipc` types derive serde traits but do not derive `Facet`, and upstream has no `Facet` feature.
- Direct facet serialization of `niri_ipc::Window`, `Workspace`, `Output`, `Event`, etc. is not currently viable without local proxy/DTO types or upstream support.
- A full facet backend would require adapter/proxy implementation for the niri IPC payload graph, so it should be treated as a separate implementation task if desired.
- Recommendation: keep serde_json as the production backend; keep `export-facet` scaffold for future experiments or upstream niri Facet support.
close_reason: Completed facet-rs research and added optional feature-gated scaffold; full backend requires separate proxy/DTO implementation if pursued.

title: Add nested field filters for export records
description: Extend export filtering beyond top-level record kind/id/type selectors to support nested field predicates such as `window.app_id=kitty`, `output.logical.width=2560`, and `cast.target.window=123`. Filters should continue to be predicates that may match zero or more records.
design: Keep existing filters (`window`, `window=4`, `type=...`) as shorthand. Add a parser representation that can handle dotted field paths, typed values, and nested enum-like payloads. Avoid hardcoding only current examples; design the matcher so additional niri_ipc fields can be added incrementally. Consider whether matching should use typed accessors, serde_json::Value projection, or a hybrid approach.
acceptance_criteria:
- Existing filters remain backward compatible.
- Nested filters can match at least window app_id, output logical dimensions, and cast target window/output.
- Invalid field paths produce useful errors.
- Tests cover zero, one, and many matches for nested predicates.
- Documentation explains that filters are ORed and can match multiple records.

title: Print stream export state on SIGUSR1
description: When running niri export streaming, support an application diagnostic signal that prints current state without stopping the stream.
design: Use SIGUSR1 on Unix as the initial signal because it is conventionally application-defined and does not imply reload or shutdown. When received during `export --stream`, emit a snapshot/state dump using the active export filters and projection options where feasible. Document that SIGUSR1 support is Unix-specific unless a later cross-platform mechanism is added.
acceptance_criteria:
- `export --stream` handles SIGUSR1 without terminating.
- Receiving SIGUSR1 emits current export state or a clearly defined snapshot record set.
- Output uses the same writer path as normal export records.
- Behavior is documented, including that SIGUSR1 is assigned by zooming-kittens and is not a niri event.
- Non-Unix behavior is explicitly handled or documented as unsupported.

title: Add unpacked stream export records
description: Add --unpack support for niri stream export so batch events can be emitted as multiple per-entity or per-change records while preserving a shared synthetic stream_event_id for regrouping.
design: Default stream output should remain faithful: one niri event becomes one output record. --unpack may split events such as WindowLayoutsChanged into one record per changed window. Include stream_event_id on unpacked records so consumers can associate records that came from the same original niri event.
acceptance_criteria:
- --unpack emits per-change/per-entity records for supported batch events.
- Unpacked records include stream_event_id.
- Default stream mode remains one output record per niri event.
- Tests cover WindowLayoutsChanged and at least one non-batch event.

title: Persist stream event id resume state
description: Add support for automatically persisting and resuming the starting stream event id for niri event exports. The stream command will initially support an explicit --starting-id with a default of 1; this follow-up should define where resume state lives, how it is keyed, and how users opt in/out of persisted counters.
design: Consider XDG state storage keyed by compositor/session/socket identity if available. The persisted id is synthetic zooming-kittens state, not a niri-provided event id. Avoid implying stability across unrelated niri sessions unless we can prove the key is safe.
acceptance_criteria:
- Users can enable persisted stream event ids without manually passing --starting-id.
- Documentation states ids are assigned by zooming-kittens and are not niri ids.
- State storage location and reset behavior are explicit.
- Tests cover starting from persisted state and resetting/overriding it.
notes: Research link: design/activity/journald-survey0.gpt6a.md (opencode://ses_e9a70537bffeI1H23pKsQ37jBa). Four-month local survey identifies Cyclrs feed-scoped opaque cursor validation as a useful selection-keying precedent, but this ticket remains synthetic ZK counter persistence, not journal resume. Umbriel owns actual activity journal follow/replay under umbrs-activity-history. Phyllited contributes binary-safe export/oracle fixtures.

title: Support additional terminals beyond kitty
description:
The zoomer and font control features are currently kitty-specific, using kitty's remote control socket protocol (via the kitty-rc crate). The core architecture (niri event stream -> resizer) is terminal-agnostic. We should add support for additional terminals.

Likely candidates:
- **Alacritty**: config-file based (requires file watch + reload, or SIGUSR1)
- **Foot**: IPC socket support, `foot --server` mode
- **WezTerm**: multiplexer API via CLI
- **Ghostty**: check available IPC

The implementation should abstract terminal interaction behind a trait so that zoomer/longcat don't need to know which terminal they're talking to. The existing KittyResizer becomes one implementation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terminal backend trait that abstracts font-size operations

title: Handle user layout modifications in longcat (window moves, etc.)
description:

title: Create shared niri connection pool for commands
description:
Currently NiriRegistry creates new connections on every focus event in get_window_info(). Each focus change triggers 2 new connections (one for focused window, one for blurred window). We need to implement a shared connection pool similar to how Longcat handles niri_socket, so that queries and actions reuse connections rather than creating new ones each time.

Key issue: src/niri/registry.rs:176 - Socket::connect() called on every get_window_info() invocation

title: Enhance zooming status JSON output with structured data
description:
Add detailed zooming status to focus event JSON output.

Currently, when kitty focus changes, we only emit basic events. We need to add structured data about font adjustment operations.

## Requirements

### Focus Gained Event
Add `zooming` field with structured status:
- `status`: "success" | "not_configured" | "connection_failed" | "auth_failed"
- `pid`: kitty process ID
- `font_adjustment`: "+3" (always)
- When successful: include adjustment details
- When failed: include error reason

Example:
```json
{
  "event": "focus_gained",
  "window_id": 12345,
  "app_id": "kitty",
  "zooming": {
    "status": "success",
    "pid": 45678,
    "font_adjustment": "+3"
  }
}
```

### Focus Lost Event
Add `zooming` field for single kitty:
- `status`: "success" | "failed"
- `pid`: kitty process ID (the one that lost focus)
- `font_adjustment`: "-3" (always)
- When failed: include error

Example:
```json
{
  "event": "focus_lost",
  "zooming": {
    "status": "success",
    "pid": 45678,
    "font_adjustment": "-3"
  }
}
```

## Notes
- Focus lost should only affect ONE kitty at a time (the one that just lost focus)
- Not all kitty instances have remote control configured
- No message field needed - use structured data only
- Status values should be machine-readable

title: Add structured JSON output mode
description:
The old README described JSON lines output to stdout, but the current code only uses eprintln for human-readable logging. We should add a proper structured JSON output mode that writes event data (focus gained/lost, font size changes, longcat height adjustments) as JSON lines to stdout. This would make the tool composable with other Unix tools and enable scripting use cases.

Acceptance criteria:
- `--output json` (or similar) flag that switches from human-readable stderr logging to structured JSON lines on stdout
- Each event type (focus, blur, font change, height change) has a defined JSON schema
- Human-readable logging stays on stderr regardless of output mode
- Existing behavior (eprintln to stderr) remains the default

title: Fix focus-lost to only affect the kitty that lost focus
description:
When focus is lost, the current implementation iterates through ALL kitty windows to decrease font size. This is incorrect - we should only affect the kitty that just lost focus.

Current buggy behavior:
- Focus lost event triggers
- Code iterates through ALL kitty windows
- Decreases font size in ALL kitty instances

Required fix:
- Track which kitty currently has focus when focus is gained
- On focus lost, only affect the kitty that just lost focus
- Clear the focus tracker after handling
